chapter: Boyhood in Webster Groves and early roadhouse work
title: Finishing grammar school; parents' $7 investment
summary: He stayed with the band from age 8 to 12. His parents worried about the cost, but his mother said to give him a chance.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And it was a nice thing. I was there from 8 to 12. I finished grammar school at 12 and my instruction I thought was tremendous. I had a chance to appreciate that later on but the funny part about it is, now you spoke about $7 being a lot of money so one thing the parents wanted to know was how do you know this boy will get to play the trumpet $7, you know. Seven dollars is $7. So they had to (schedule) it as my mother and father always did. She said, 'Well, give him a chance.' And after they saw my interest, you know, they (paid) it.
Well, from their point of view, it was a darn good investment because it gave you something to interest you, didn't it? as you grew up?
It did, it really and truly did.
